questions.title: Linked List Length
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (input reading, Node class and chain building) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def list_length(head):

head is the head Node of a singly linked chain (each node has value and next). Return the number of nodes by walking the chain.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of nodes.
Line 2: n integers — the node values in chain order.

Output Format:
One line with the number of nodes.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
-1000000 <= value <= 1000000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.next = None


def build_chain(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def chain_values(head):
    out = []
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out

def list_length(head):
    count = 0
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        count += 1
        node = node.next
    return count


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    head = build_chain(values)
    print(list_length(head))


main()

class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):

import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.next = None


def build_chain(values):

    tail = None

questions.title: Cycle Detection by Floyd
questions.description:
A ticket chain has looped somewhere and the auditor runs Floyd's tortoise-and-hare: slow moves one link per step, fast moves two; they must meet iff a cycle exists. Naming matters on this floor — use the variables slow and fast.

The program scaffolding (input reading, Node class and chain building) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def has_cycle(head):

head is the head Node of the chain; the harness has already linked the tail back to a node when the input says so. Return True when the chain contains a cycle, False otherwise, using the slow/fast two-pointer method. Storing visited nodes is banned — the grader rejects set( and dict(.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of nodes.
Line 2: n integers — the node values in chain order.
Line 3: pos: the 0-based index the tail loops back to, or -1 when the chain is linear.

Output Format:
One line with True or False.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
-1 <= pos < n
-1000000 <= value <= 1000000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.next = None


def build_chain(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def chain_values(head):
    out = []
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out

def build_chain_with_cycle(values, pos):
    head = build_chain(values)
    if pos >= 0:
        tail = head
        while tail.next is not None:
            tail = tail.next
        target = head
        steps = pos
        while steps > 0:
            target = target.next
            steps -= 1
        tail.next = target
    return head

def has_cycle(head):
    slow = head
    fast = head
    while fast is not None and fast.next is not None:
        slow = slow.next
        fast = fast.next.next
        if slow is fast:
            return True
    return False


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    pos = int(data[1 + n])
    head = build_chain_with_cycle(values, pos)
    print(has_cycle(head))


main()

Two depots ship chains of parcels, each already ascending by priority. The control room splices them into ONE ascending chain by re-linking nodes — no re-sorting.

The program scaffolding (input reading, Node class and chain building) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def merge_chains(head1, head2):

head1 and head2 are the head Nodes of two ascending chains. Return the head of the merged ascending chain built from the SAME nodes (a dummy head node makes the splicing easy — Node is available). The harness prints the merged chain.

Input Format:

Constraints:

questions.sourcecode:
import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.next = None


def build_chain(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def chain_values(head):
    out = []
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out

def merge_chains(head1, head2):
    dummy = Node(0)
    tail = dummy
    a, b = head1, head2
    while a is not None and b is not None:
        if a.value <= b.value:
            tail.next = a
            a = a.next
        else:
            tail.next = b
            b = b.next
        tail = tail.next
    if a is not None:
        tail.next = a
    else:
        tail.next = b
    return dummy.next


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n1 = int(data[0])
    a = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n1]))
    n2 = int(data[1 + n1])
    b = list(map(int, data[2 + n1:2 + n1 + n2]))
    head1 = build_chain(a)
    head2 = build_chain(b)
    merged = merge_chains(head1, head2)
    print(' '.join(map(str, chain_values(merged))))


main()

import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.next = None


def build_chain(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def chain_values(head):
    out = []
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out

def build_chain_with_cycle(values, pos):
    head = build_chain(values)
    if pos >= 0:
        tail = head
        while tail.next is not None:
            tail = tail.next
        target = head
        steps = pos
        while steps > 0:
            target = target.next
            steps -= 1
        tail.next = target
    return head

def cycle_start(head):
    slow = head
    fast = head
    while fast is not None and fast.next is not None:
        slow = slow.next
        fast = fast.next.next
        if slow is fast:
            finder = head
            while finder is not slow:
                finder = finder.next
                slow = slow.next
            return finder.value
    return -1


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    pos = int(data[1 + n])
    head = build_chain_with_cycle(values, pos)
    print(cycle_start(head))


main()

questions.title: Reverse Checkpoints in Blocks
questions.description:
A memory pager reverses its checkpoint chain in blocks of k: every full group of k consecutive nodes is reversed, and a leftover tail shorter than k stays untouched (k = 1 leaves everything as-is).

The program scaffolding (input reading, Node class and chain building) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def reverse_groups(head, k):

head is the head Node of the checkpoint chain. Reverse the chain in groups of exactly k nodes and return the NEW head. The harness prints the resulting chain.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of checkpoints.
Line 2: n integers — the checkpoint ids in chain order.
Line 3: the block size k (1 <= k <= n + 4).

Output Format:
One line with the reordered checkpoints, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
1 <= k <= n + 4
-1000000 <= value <= 1000000

import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.next = None


def build_chain(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def chain_values(head):
    out = []
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out

def reverse_groups(head, k):
    node = head
    count = 0
    while node is not None:
        count += 1
        node = node.next
    new_head = None
    prev_tail = None
    curr = head
    while count >= k:
        group_head = curr
        prev = None
        i = 0
        while i < k:
            nxt = curr.next
            curr.next = prev
            prev = curr
            curr = nxt
            i += 1
        if new_head is None:
            new_head = prev
        else:
            prev_tail.next = prev
        prev_tail = group_head
        count -= k
    if prev_tail is not None:
        prev_tail.next = curr
    if new_head is None:
        return head
    return new_head


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    k = int(data[1 + n])
    head = build_chain(values)
    head = reverse_groups(head, k)
    print(' '.join(map(str, chain_values(head))))


main()
